title.narrative: NESA Center Indo-Pacific Forum 01-25: "Underwater and Maritime Domain Awareness and Technological Innovation in the Indo-Pacific"

description.narrative: The maritime domain is the source of much of the Indo-Pacifics material wealth, diplomatic energy, and even its regional disputes. The underwater domain is a key variable for understanding the dynamics of the Indo-Pacific and gaining awareness of the variables underwater is the objective of this program. This effort, a cooperative program between NESA, DKI APCSS, and the Gordian Knot Center at Stanford University, seeks to explore the underwater domain. Topics to be explored include the security of undersea cables, the prospects of seabed mining, the technological tools and applications that are being deployed beneath the surface, ways greater security beneath the surface can be achieved in partnerships of various types, and the approaches through which various regional states conceive of underwater security concerns, among others. The event is a Track 1.5 Effort, where official representatives from regional governments will join subject matter experts, scientists, commercial firms, technology companies, and strategists. The event follows the Chatham House rule of non-attribution and will take place on the campus of Stanford University in Palo Alto, California. The event will feature both panels and small group tabletop scenarios. Following the event, the organizers will craft a report of the events proceedings and its findings that will be shared with all participants and cooperating institutions.
